title: Choose a Minecraft-like world
question: You rejected the timetable. Binding vibe: Minecraft (blocks, inventory, dirt/stone/grass, chunky pixels). Same job: stack periods from a start time, 15-minute buffer, +15, export to Calendar. Code-led — pick a card to build.

options.label: Pause screen
options.thesis: The day is a dirt-field pause menu: stone-brick buttons, one hotspot row, Done writes the world to Calendar.
options.viewport: Full-bleed dirt. Title is today’s date in chunky type. Periods are a vertical stack of stone buttons with clocks on the left. Hotbar of stamps along the bottom. Done = Post to Calendar.
options.risk: Reads as a settings screen if the buttons stay generic ‘options’ instead of timed blocks.

raised.raise: One bitmap face, only two sizes. No third font.
Color lives on the grass rim of a block, not a page wash.
One biome sky. Do not switch worlds mid-day.

options.label: Hotbar day
options.thesis: Each intention is a stack in the hotbar. The selected slot is the live block; +15 grows the stack; the day is what you are holding.
options.viewport: Center: the held block with its clock. Bottom: 9 slots (stamps + filled periods). XP bar under the hotbar is the 15-minute buffer. Inventory key opens the full list. Export is ‘Save & Quit to Calendar’.
options.risk: This is the most familiar Minecraft UI. It can look like a texture pack on a todo list if the slots are stickers.

options.label: Explorer map
options.thesis: The overworld map is the sheet. Periods are purple control points. +15 redraws the course line.
options.viewport: Beige map filling the iPad. Numbered purple circles are periods. Legend = stamps. Copy map = Calendar.
options.case: Beats pause-menu on identification (you already asked for Minecraft) and on clarity (a course you can read).
options.risk: Looks like a gimmick map if the purple line is decoration and the times live in a sidebar.

options.label: Item rail
options.lineage: Film cutting bench as an item rail
options.thesis: Periods hang on a hopper rail like items on a track. The flag is where you stopped. +15 punches the next frames forward.
options.viewport: One horizontal rail of item frames at mid-height. Stamps sit in a chest row under it. Export unloads the rail.
options.case: Holds clarity (sequence on a rail). Identification only after Minecraft translation; as film it would lose.
options.risk: A long rail on iPad can become a tiny strip of icons without clocks.

options.label: Item catalog
options.lineage: Character-goods grid as a double chest
options.thesis: Presets are items in a chest grid. The day is the hotbar you fill from that chest.
options.viewport: Double-chest of stamps on top; the day’s taken items in a row beneath. Tooltip shows clock times. Close chest exports.
options.case: Holds identification (inventory is home). Loses some clarity: times hide in tooltips unless printed on the slot.
options.risk: If times are only in hover, the iPad job fails.

options.label: Void scroller
options.thesis: The day is a bitmap ticker on black, with no boxes.
options.viewport: Black void, scrolling period names, clocks as gold dust.
options.risk: You cannot tap a block that is not there.
options.case: Minecraft is boxes. A boxless void fails the pin and hides clocks.
options.kept: One pixel face, two sizes only.

options.label: Cloud edge
options.thesis: The day dissolves into a pastel weather wash.
options.viewport: Pale sky, periods as cloud labels.
options.risk: Looks like the AI weather app, not a block world.
options.case: Weather pastel is not a block game.
options.kept: Accent only on a block’s rim.

options.label: Gravity garden
options.thesis: Periods fall upward through a dusk garden.
options.viewport: Night plants, times raining the wrong way.
options.risk: Pretty, and useless for stacking a morning.
options.case: Surreal rain is not this planner and not Minecraft.
options.kept: One biome; do not change worlds mid-day.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A calm split-view planner. The AI default you asked to leave.
canonCard.risk: Looks generated. You already rejected this family.
